clue.text: Democrat's explanatory writing about a regressive old tax

indicators.note: regressive means going backwards, so the whole assembled string is read in reverse

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for a Democrat

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the explanatory writing goes round the article

parts.note: a legend is the explanatory caption or key on a map or picture

explanation.surface: A Democrat writes an explanation of an old tax that hits the poor hardest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside LEGEND to make LEGENAD; with D in front that is DLEGENAD, and 'regressive' reads it all backwards. 'Regressive' pretends to be the economist's word for a tax.
explanation.definitionFit: The historical levy raised in Anglo-Saxon England to buy off Viking raiders is the classic example of an old tax.

clue.text: Mixed pairs do a race round the world

indicators.note: mixed signals that the letters of pairs do a are jumbled

explanation.surface: Mixed doubles pairs run a round-the-world race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'race' is not a contest but a people, scattered across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispersion is a people scattered from their homeland across many countries, as the Jewish people were.

clue.text: Wise to put by new material

indicators.note: put by means placed beside, so the abbreviation for new sits next to the phrase

parts.note: to be wise to something is to be in on it

explanation.surface: A sensible person saves up to buy new fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put by' looks like saving; it means placed beside.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a lightweight sheer fabric of silk or nylon, used for dresses and curtains.

clue.text: Need wise words to be clear

parts.note: to need something is to go without it
a saying is a proverb, wise words

explanation.surface: Wise words are needed to make the point plain.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is self-evident needs no stating, so it is perfectly obvious.

clue.text: Launch cancelled after end of hitch-hiking

indicators.note: after says the word for cancelled follows the hitch-hiker's goal

parts.note: the end or purpose of hitch-hiking is getting a lift
an event that is cancelled is off

explanation.surface: A hitch-hiking trip is called off at the last stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' wants to take a last letter; here it means the aim of hitch-hiking.
explanation.definitionFit: The moment a rocket leaves the pad is its launch.

clue.text: Trim Christmas tree

explanation.surface: A neatly cut fir ready for the festive season.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance; as a noun it is the conifer commonly brought indoors at Christmas.

clue.text: It prevents rocky ground becoming really stony

indicators.note: ground means crushed up, so the letters of it prevents rocky are reshaped

explanation.surface: A crop fails because rocky soil turns to stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'really stony' means utterly broke (stony broke), not full of stones.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony broke means penniless, so very poor.

clue.text: Balaclava fellow from Britain drops in surrounding area

parts.note: UK is the United Kingdom, so from Britain
rain falls in drops

indicators.note: surrounding means in goes round the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A man in a balaclava from Britain drops into the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: Balaclava is not the woolly hat but the town in Crimea, scene of the Charge of the Light Brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: Balaclava is a town in Crimea, so a native of it is a citizen of that country.

clue.text: Spaniard no longer with man U quits team

indicators.note: no longer with means the named letters are taken away from the Spaniard

parts.note: Manuel is a Spanish name, such as the waiter in Fawlty Towers
when debts are settled the parties are quits, or even

explanation.surface: A Spanish player leaves Manchester United and quits the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man U' looks like the football club but is the four letters to remove from MANUEL, leaving EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A football or cricket side has that many players, so the number names a team.

clue.text: Was father holding book when rearing litter?

indicators.note: rearing means rising up, so in this down clue the letters are read bottom to top
holding means the letter for book is held inside

parts.note: to have sired is to have been father to offspring

explanation.surface: Was father reading a book while bringing up a litter of young?
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' puts B in SIRED to make SIRBED, and 'rearing' turns it upwards. 'rearing' and 'litter' suggest animals breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Litter is scattered rubbish, the same as remains or wreckage strewn about.

clue.text: Like today's article anticipating wintry weather

indicators.note: anticipating means coming before, so the article goes in front of the weather

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
snow is typical wintry weather

explanation.surface: Like the article in today's paper forecasting a cold snap.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done in the same way as at present is done as it is currently, the way of today.

clue.text: Following battle's ending in defeat, liberated lines

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references

indicators.note: in places the battle's last letter inside the word for defeat

parts.note: a reverse is a setback or defeat

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of battle's

explanation.surface: After a battle ends in defeat, the prisoners are freed and the poetry flows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' gives E, the last letter of battle's, which goes inside REVERSE after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Poetry without regular metre or rhyme is verse released from the usual constraints, so its lines are liberated.

clue.text: Fruit portion in crumbles

indicators.note: crumbles signals the letters of portion in falling apart and reforming

explanation.surface: A serving of fruit inside the crumble puddings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit' and 'crumbles' suggest a pudding; the definition is the grape variety (and its wine), a sneaky use of 'Fruit'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a black grape variety grown for red wine, so a fruit of the vine.

clue.text: Rave over, heading off for rally

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter is removed from the word meaning rave over

parts.note: to rave over something is to praise it

explanation.surface: After the party is over, the crowd heads off to a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally support or funds is to gather or raise them.

clue.text: Dressing down in sort of cloth top

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery and ties
a roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: Someone being told off while wearing a top made of a particular fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing down is a stern rebuke or telling-off.

clue.text: Length of cloth used in fitting attachment on aircraft

indicators.note: used in means the length unit is placed inside the word for fitting

parts.note: proper means fitting or suitable
an ell is an old measure of cloth length

explanation.surface: A length of fabric used to fit something onto a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating bladed screw is fitted to many aircraft to drive them through the air.

clue.text: Snooker break is met with incredulity in the end

indicators.note: break signals the letters being broken up and rearranged
in the end picks the final letter of incredulity

explanation.surface: A snooker break meets with disbelief at the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' and 'Snooker' paint a snooker table, but the definition is the verb: to snooker someone is to obstruct them. 'in the end' gives Y, the last letter of incredulity, which joins ISMET in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: To snooker someone is to leave them blocked or thwarted, as is to obstruct a golfer's putt.

clue.text: Time needed to build a large audience?

explanation.surface: How long it takes to gather a big crowd of listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: Split differently, the answer reads as lots of ears, a big audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Work time is measured in units of one person working a year, as needed for building; a crowd of listeners has numerous ears.

clue.text: Spa feature perhaps too much in activity centre

indicators.note: in puts the phrase for too much inside the centre

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity
OTT stands for over the top, meaning too much

explanation.surface: A spa offers rather too much at its activity centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated outdoor bath of bubbling water is a typical attraction at a spa, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Tramp over land, pouch fitted to belt

indicators.note: over means placed above in this down clue, so the tramp sits on top

parts.note: a bum is a tramp or vagrant
to bag a fish or prize is to land it

explanation.surface: A tramp walking across country wears a pouch on his belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A small zipped bag worn round the waist on a strap is a pouch on a belt.

clue.text: Barrel one enveloped in a variety of green flower

indicators.note: enveloped in means wrapped inside the colour word

parts.note: pea green is a shade of green, so pea names a variety of green
a tun is a large barrel for wine or beer
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A barrel stuffed with greenery to grow a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a garden bedding plant with trumpet-shaped blooms, a species of flower.

clue.text: Spiv accepting tips harbouring admission of guilt

indicators.note: tips means upends, so in this down clue the hidden letters are turned upwards
harbouring means the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A spiv taking backhanders while keeping a confession to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'harbouring' takes IVACCEP from inside 'Spiv accepting', and 'tips' upends those letters. 'tips' looks like bribes for the spiv.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'I have sinned', it is used as a confession of wrongdoing.

clue.text: Periodically awaits ad — forms judgment

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken from the words

explanation.surface: Someone waits for an advertisement and forms an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sound judgment is good sense, the quality of being sagacious.

clue.text: Girl, one with title again spurning me

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: spurning means rejecting, so the letters of me are thrown out

parts.note: to rename something is to give it a title again

explanation.surface: A girl given her title once more refuses to have me involved.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female forename, so a girl's name.

clue.text: Plant stunted pine in pit by track

indicators.note: in puts the shortened word for pine inside the pit

parts.note: a mine is a pit

indicators.note: stunted means cut short, so the last letter of the word for pine is dropped

parts.note: to pine is to ache or long for something
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a track

explanation.surface: A dwarf pine growing in a quarry beside a railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' and 'pine' push towards trees; plant here means industrial equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant in industry means the machines and heavy equipment used in a process.

clue.text: Fleet street pursuing English artist

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the fleet and street come after English

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is a fleet

explanation.surface: An English artist working on Fleet Street, London's old newspaper home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fleet street' looks like London's former newspaper district, but the words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Max Ernst was a German surrealist painter, so an artist.

clue.text: Religious leader from a west African country a boy repelled

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: Mali is a country in west Africa
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A religious leader turns away a boy from West Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' reverses all of A MALI A LAD, giving DAL A ILAM A.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism, so a religious leader.

clue.text: Informal sort of family lawyer

parts.note: kin are one's family
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A family lawyer, more or less.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual spoken contraction meaning somewhat or more or less, the informal form of 'kind of'.

clue.text: After mass I see red vision

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the abbreviation for mass

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics
to see red is to be in a rage

explanation.surface: After church, someone sees red visions.
explanation.definitionFit: An optical illusion in the desert is an apparition, a deceptive vision.

clue.text: Groan perhaps about pub that's buzzing

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the name goes round the pub

parts.note: Titus Groan is the hero of Mervyn Peake's Gormenghast novels, so Groan is a surname of someone called Titus
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A groan about a lively pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Groan' looks like a noise; it is the surname of Mervyn Peake's character Titus Groan.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a medical condition of ringing or humming in the ears, a persistent buzzing.
